# Keymap

<!-- GENERATED by tools/keymap.mjs — do not edit by hand. -->

Every keybinding on this machine, read from the configs themselves.

Keys are delivered top-down through these layers. Whoever claims a combination
first consumes it, so anything below with the same combination never sees the
keystroke:

| # | layer | scope |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `karabiner` | remaps at the HID level, before any application sees the key |
| 2 | `aerospace` | global hotkeys — claimed system-wide, in every application |
| 3 | `cmux` | the terminal application, when it is frontmost |
| 4 | `vscode` | the editor, when it is frontmost |
| 5 | `ghostty` | the terminal surface, inside cmux |
| 6 | `pi` | the TUI, inside that surface |

`✦` below is Hyper — `⌃⌥⌘` together, bound to Caps Lock in Karabiner.

## Shadowed bindings

None. No binding is claimed by a layer above the one that defines it.

## Karabiner rules without a simple trigger

These use nested manipulators or variable conditions, so no single combination
could be extracted. Listed for completeness:

- Hyper Key + Double tap Escape
- Vim Mode: Escape → desactiva vim_mode
- Vim Mode: hjkl → arrows
- Vim Mode: w/b → word navigation
- Vim Mode: x → delete char
- Vim Mode: i → insert mode (exit vim mode)
- Vim Mode: a → append (exit vim mode, move right)

---

Regenerate with `node tools/keymap.mjs`. `--check` fails if either output is
stale or if a shadowed binding exists.

`chrome/keymap/` is the same data as a Chrome extension that overrides the New
Tab page. It must work with no network at all.
